title_en: The vision described in the surah of the star
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. The occasions of revelation (who the persons were, what happened) are not in the verses; they appear only under unknowns and uncertainties, as later tradition, with the hadith to add later. Pronouns the Arabic leaves open are left open. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

chapters.title_en: The companion who has not strayed

claims.statement_en: God swears by the star when it falls.
God says that the companion of those addressed has neither strayed nor erred.
He does not speak out of desire.
It is nothing but a revelation that is being revealed.

chapters.summary_md: God swears by the star when it falls [c1]. He says that the companion of those addressed has neither strayed nor erred [c2], and that he does not speak out of desire [c3]. It is nothing but a revelation being revealed [c4].
chapters.body_md:
God swears by the star when it falls [c1].

He says that the companion of those addressed has neither strayed nor erred [c2]. He does not speak out of desire [c3]. It is nothing but a revelation that is being revealed [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The passage opens with an oath and then makes a series of statements about the companion [c1][c2][c3]. The last statement says what 'it' is, and does so by the word revelation [c4]. The verse does not say what 'it' refers to [c4].
chapters.kids_md: God swears by the star when it falls [c1]. God says that the companion has not strayed and has not erred [c2]. He does not speak out of desire [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage separates what is said out of desire from what is revealed [c3][c4]. Another is that it begins by setting the companion's honesty before anything else is said [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the companion is. The verse says 'your companion' and gives no name.
- Not established: what 'it' refers to in 53:4, or whether 'the star when it falls' is a star, a group of stars, or something else; the Arabic word and its verb are read in more than one way.
- Not established: when or where the words were first heard.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the companion and the occasion. Neither is used in the story texts.

claims.statement_en: The companion was taught by one who is strong in power.
God revealed to His servant what He revealed.
The heart did not lie about what it saw.
The verse asks the listeners whether they will dispute with him about what he sees.

chapters.summary_md: The passage says that the companion was taught by one who is strong in power [c1]. It says that God revealed to His servant what He revealed [c2], that the heart did not lie about what it saw [c3], and asks whether they will dispute with him about what he sees [c4].
chapters.body_md:
The passage says that the companion was taught by one who is strong in power [c1].

It says that God revealed to His servant what He revealed [c2]. The heart did not lie about what it saw [c3]. The verse then asks the listeners whether they will dispute with him about what he sees [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The passage names a teacher only by a quality, strong in power, and does not name him [c1]. It does not say what God revealed, only that He revealed what He revealed [c2]. It speaks of the heart and of what was seen, and of a dispute about what is seen [c3][c4].
chapters.kids_md: The passage says that the companion was taught by one who is strong in power [c1]. God revealed to His servant what He revealed [c2]. The verses say that his heart did not lie about what it saw [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage treats what was revealed and what was seen as true and asks the listeners not to dispute it [c3][c4]. Another is that it leaves what was revealed unspecified [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the teacher is. The verses give a quality and no name; later readers differ on who is meant, and the draft takes no side.
- Not established: who 'his servant' is, what was revealed to him, or what the heart saw; the verses say 'what He revealed' and 'what it saw'.
- This chapter leaves out 53:6-9, which speak of where the teacher stood and how near he came. They are left out on purpose, because they invite a picture; a scholar should decide whether the page should present them and in what words.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the teacher and of the one who saw. Neither is used in the story texts.

chapters.title_en: At the lote tree of the farthest limit

claims.statement_en: The verse says that he saw him on another descent, a word that can also be read as another occasion.
It was at the lote tree of the farthest limit, near which is the garden of refuge.
This was when the lote tree was covered by what covered it.
The sight did not swerve and did not exceed.
He saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord.

chapters.summary_md: The passage says that he saw him on another descent [c1], at the lote tree of the farthest limit, near which is the garden of refuge [c2]. It says that the sight did not swerve and did not exceed [c4], and that he saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord [c5].
chapters.body_md:
The passage says that he saw him on another descent, a word that can also be read as another occasion [c1].

It was at the lote tree of the farthest limit, near which is the garden of refuge [c2]. This was when the lote tree was covered by what covered it [c3].

The sight did not swerve and did not exceed [c4]. He saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The passage does not say who is seen; the pronoun is not resolved in the verse [c1]. It names a place by its names, the lote tree of the farthest limit and the garden of refuge [c2]. What covered the lote tree is not said [c3]. The passage closes with what the sight did not do and with what was seen, signs of his Lord [c4][c5].
chapters.kids_md: The passage says that he saw something on another occasion [c1]. It was at the lote tree of the farthest limit, near the garden of refuge [c2]. He saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord [c5].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage describes what was seen as signs of the Lord and not as an end in itself [c5]. Another is that it speaks of a sight that did not swerve and did not exceed [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: whom he saw, or what he saw. The pronoun in 53:13 is not resolved here, and 'the greatest signs' are not listed.
- Not established: what covered the lote tree, where the tree is, or what 'the farthest limit' is a limit of.
- Not established: when this took place or how it relates to any journey; the verses do not say.
- The Arabic word for 'descent' can be read as a descent or as an occasion; the draft gives both.
- This chapter does not describe the one seen or the manner of the sight, and no verse here does.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the one seen and the occasion. Neither is used in the story texts.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the vision, on the identity of the one who taught and the one seen, and on the occasion, each with a named grader. None is used in this draft.

This story is drafted with the greatest restraint. It states only what the verses say, names no angel, describes no one, and leaves out 53:6-9, which speak of position and nearness. A scholar should decide whether and how to include them.
Whether the one who taught (53:5) and the one seen (53:13) are the same, and who they are, is a question the verses leave to interpretation; the draft does not decide it.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identity of the companion, of the teacher and of the one seen, and the occasion of the passage.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.
